subject: Serving-mode fit assessment — PoC sprint plan
summary: Post-discovery follow-up to clarify deployment-mode fit (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). External requests on data residency and audit logs push toward Private/VPC evaluation; we propose a 4-week PoC sprint with clear success criteria, stakeholders, and a fallback to Dedicated if VPC timeline slips.
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Carter Taylor <ctaylor@medisure.com>
Cc: Patricia Martinez <pmartinez@medisure.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Serving-mode fit assessment — next steps from today's call

Carter / Patricia,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and the actions I promised: we discussed three potential serving modes for your inference workloads: Hosted API (fastest onboarding), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput, shared control plane), and Private VPC / on-prem (full network isolation and customer-managed control plane).

What you told us that matters for the decision:
- P1: Patient data residency requirements for some pilot customers — Indian and EU data must not leave region.
- P2: Auditability — you need request-level audit logs and keys managed by your KMS.
- P3: Expected peak throughput is ~20 qps for batch policy scoring and occasional sync inference within the UI (99th pct latency target ~300ms).

Given the above, Private VPC looks like the most compliant-fit but will require some lead time (networking, KMS integration, and access reviews). Dedicated could be a pragmatic near-term option if you need predictable throughput and faster ramp while we stand up the VPC work. Hosted API would be easiest for an initial feature test, but it doesn't meet the KMS/residency constraints you described.

Attached are my discovery notes + the spreadsheet you provided with the compliance checklist (I've redacted a few fields). Proposed next step: run a 4-week PoC sprint that validates two things in parallel — (A) Dedicated-capacity PoC for performance/latency and cost profiling, and (B) VPC feasibility track (network + KMS + audit logs). If the VPC track clears by week 3 we pivot the PoC to a VPC-centric pilot; if not, we finalize on Dedicated for launch and schedule the VPC onboarding for a second-phase migration.

Requesting the following from your side to lock the PoC:
1) A single point of contact for networking/KMS (name + email)
2) Test dataset samples (PII redacted where needed) and a short list of the top 15 prompt templates used in scoring
3) Confirmation that a staging VPC peering window is available within the next 3 weeks (if you want VPC on the track)

I'll draft a one-page PoC sprint plan with owners and milestones and loop Marissa and Karthik for specific resource commitments (engineer time, infra).

Thanks,
Vivek
Vice President, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20260927-discovery-notes.pdf (PDF, 42KB); medisure-security-constraints.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

From: Carter Taylor <ctaylor@medisure.com>

Cc: Patricia Martinez <pmartinez@medisure.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T18:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Serving-mode fit assessment — next steps from today's call

Vivek,

Appreciate the clear recap — that's aligned with our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Data residency: our EU pilots need to ensure at-rest and in-transit controls remain within EU for dataset subsets; however, some telemetry for usage can be aggregated outside as long as it's anonymized.
- KMS: we run keys in AWS KMS (alias/medisure-prod); we require envelope encryption with customer-managed keys and proof of key usage in audit logs.
- Timeline: our launch target for the first pilot is end of Q1 2027. We can carve out engineering bandwidth for a PoC starting mid-October.

Points of contact:
- Networking & Security lead: Patricia Martinez <pmartinez@medisure.com> (cc'd)
- ML infra contact: Alex Lopez <alopez@medisure.com> (will be on subsequent threads)

We like the two-track approach you proposed. For prioritization: if Dedicated gives us throughput guarantees quickly, that is acceptable as a temporary step, but VPC is the long-term requirement. One ask: can Redwood provide a checklist of the network ports and peering requirements so Patricia can run the initial approval? Also please include a short list of what evidence we can expect for audit logging (S3, CloudTrail events, etc.).

Thanks,
Carter
Head of MLOps
MediSure Inc.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Carter Taylor <ctaylor@medisure.com>
Cc: Patricia Martinez <pmartinez@medisure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: PoC sprint plan (Medisure) — 4-week proposal + success metrics

Carter / Patricia,

Following our thread and internal alignment, attached is the proposed PoC sprint outline. High level:
- Duration: 4 weeks (two-track with a VPC feasibility lane and Dedicated perf lane)
- Week 0 (prep, signoffs): networking checklist, account access, staging data handoff, contact list
- Week 1 (Dedicated baseline): deploy dedicated capacity, run baseline throughput/latency tests with provided prompts/datasets
- Week 2 (VPC setup & KMS): networking peering window, KMS key wrapping tests, audit log validation (sample CloudTrail events + request-level traces)
- Week 3 (integration & validation): run full workload, compare p95/p99 latency, verify audit evidence and residency controls on sample datasets
- Week 4 (report & next steps): finalize evaluation report, cost/perf tradeoffs, recommended deployment path and migration timeline

Success criteria (any two of the three):
- Performance: p95 latency <= 300ms for UI calls and 15 qps sustained for scoring batch jobs on Dedicated baseline or better on VPC
- Compliance: ability to demonstrate customer-managed KMS integration and audit logs for a sample of requests
- Operational: end-to-end deployment repeatable by your infra team and an agreed plan for rolling to production within 8 weeks after PoC (if Dedicated chosen)

Owners & contacts:
- Redwood technical lead: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com) — PoC engineer and test runner
- Redwood infra lead: Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwood.com) — VPC & KMS integration
- Medisure networking/security: Patricia Martinez (pmartinez@medisure.com)
- Medisure ML infra: Alex Lopez (alopez@medisure.com) — onboarding of test models/datasets

If this looks good, we'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff with Patricia and Alex next week and confirm the peering window. If you prefer, we can start the Dedicated baseline first (it can be provisioned within 72 hours) while the VPC approvals run.

Deliverables attached: one-page PoC brief, network checklist matrix, and an example audit evidence sample (redacted).

Next asks from your side to begin:
1) Confirm Patricia and Alex as primary contacts for the kickoff
2) Share a redacted sample dataset and the list of 10-15 prompt templates
3) Confirm whether you want us to provision Dedicated baseline immediately (we can provision once we have buyoff)

I'll await your confirmation and will book the kickoff slot for next week (tentative: Tue 10/05 10am PT).

Best,
Vivek
Vice President, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: PoC-brief-onepager.pdf (PDF, 24KB); network-peering-checklist.csv (CSV, 6KB); audit-evidence-sample.txt (TXT, 8KB)
